We argue, in parallel with Gallager's (1968) proof for the equivalence of channel capacity and minimum redundancy in data compression, that both problems have the same answer min/sub b/ max/sub /spl theta// /spl int/p/sub /spl theta//lnb/sub /spl theta///sup t/x/b/sup t/x.

articleTitle: Many non-abelian groups support only group codes that are conformant to abelian group codes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Define a group code C over a group (G,*,1) to be a subgroup of the sequence space G/sup Z/ that is stationary and is not also a subgroup of a sequence space defined on a proper subgroup of G. In addition, consider group codes to be finitely-controllable and complete. This implies that there exist minimal sets of finite-length encoder sequences that will causally encode the group code like an impulse response system over the group G. A non-abelian group code is a group code over a non-abelian group. Two group codes, C/sub 1/ over G/sub 1/ and C/sub 2/ over G/sub 2/, are defined to be conformant if there exists a bijective mapping between the group codes, /spl psi//sub /spl infin//:C/sub 1//spl rarr/C/sub 2/, such that it is the component-wise application of a group bijection /spl psi/:G/sub 1//spl rarr/G/sub 2/ (and with /spl psi/(1)=l).

articleTitle: Cyclic two dimensional IT reducing codes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Multitrack recording codes achieve larger storage capacities than separately applied single-track codes. Beside the ordinary intratrack (d) and the global (k) phrase length constraints, a radial (dy) constraint should be introduced. In order to increase immunity to intertrack interference by coding, an additional radial (dy) constraint must be imposed on coded sequences. An ordinary dy-constraint would lead to lower recording densities for the inner than for the outer tracks. A modified, cyclic radial constraint which solves these problems is proposed. Channel capacities and spectra of these codes are also presented.

articleTitle: Arbitrarily varying multiple-access channels. I. Ericson's symmetrizability is adequate, Gubner's conjecture is true
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Ericson's conjecture has been established by Csiszar and Narayan (1988). In the theory of identification the cycle closes: both, the non-single letter separability by random words and symmetrizability are used and needed. Gubner extends the decoding rule of Csiszar and Narayan to the multiple-access situation by following "conditional decoding". This is a suboptimal decoding rule, but was suited for the discovery of the capacity theorem for the multiple-access channel (MAC). Its drawback for systems of channels was soon realized by Ahlswede (1974), where for the derivation of the capacity theorem for the compound MAC maximum likelihood decoding could be analysed. For the arbitrarily varying MAC (AVMAC) suboptimality of the conditional decoding rule becomes even more significant. The authors examine if Gubner's conjecture is true.

articleTitle: Minimum description length prediction of next symbol
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: The paper shows that the known "add-half" rule is not asymptotically optimal for minimal description length prediction of the (n+1)-st symbol after a sequence of n symbols, whereas the "add-/spl beta//sub 0/",/spl beta//sub 0/=0.50922 rule is. We also estimate from below the performance of arbitrary, not just "add-something" prediction.

articleTitle: Image coding over real/complex fields: parameters estimation of nearly nonstationary AR(p) models
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: The AR parameter estimation problem is considered under noisy conditions concerned with the decoding of BCH codes over real/-complex fields. Autoregressive parameter distribution based on the parameter covariance matrix is analyzed. This distribution defines the code ability to correct the impulse noise in spectral coefficients corrupted by white noise.

articleTitle: Application of the squaring construction to PSK constellations
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: A systematic procedure for the decoding of codes obtained through the squaring construction is proposed. It was employed to evaluate the performance of codes based on PSK constellations.

articleTitle: High-resolution source coding for non-difference distortion measures: the rate distortion function
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: The problem of asymptotic (i.e., low-distortion) behavior of the rate-distortion function of a random vector is investigated for a class of non-difference distortion measures. The main result is an asymptotically tight expression which parallels the Shannon lower bound for difference distortion measures. Applications include remote source coding and high resolution quantization theory for non-difference distortion measures.

articleTitle: Performance of joint spatial and temporal multiuser detection using adaptive array antenna in both transmitter and receiver for DS/CDMA
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: This paper examines the case where a transmitter and receiver array antenna is used as a part of the physical channel. Since the array antenna is used as a filtering tool, the design of the transmitter and receiver is considered in both the space and time domains. This paper describes a design scheme of the transmitter and receiver antenna weight from the view point of signal processing.

articleTitle: Iterative multiuser detection of a multiple access FSK system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: The performance of a collision frequency shift keying system (CFSK) multiple access system is investigated. In CFSK two or more users can simultaneously transmit the same frequency resulting in a collision. A new iterative consensus decoder, the maximum a posteriori consensus decoder, is formulated and the performance investigated in the presence of noise. In this decoder, each user uses a maximum a posteriori decoding algorithm to calculate the probability that they transmitted each of the frequencies. The resulting probability distributions are then shared among the users and refined by iteration. This decoder is based on the derivation of a metric for the noisy CFSK channel. Simulation results demonstrate the efficacy of the new decoder.

articleTitle: New binary sequence sets with favourable correlations
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We construct new families of pseudorandom binary sequences from Legendre sequences and MDS codes. We obtain, for p=4k-1 prime and t an integer with 1/spl les/t/spl les/(p-1)/2, a set of p/sup t/ binary sequences of period p/sup 2/ whose peak correlation is bounded by 1+2t(p+1). The sequences are balanced, have high linear complexity and are easily generated.

articleTitle: On the maximum number of systematically-encoded information bits in the Varshamov-Tenengol'ts codes and the Constantin-Rao codes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Although Constantin-Rao (1979) codes are at least as large as Varshamov-Tenengol'ts (1965) codes of the same length, we show that CR codes cannot systematically encode more bits than VT codes.

articleTitle: Symbol-by-symbol MAP decoding of convolutional codes using reciprocal dual convolutional codes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: A new symbol-by-symbol maximum a-posteriori (MAP) decoding algorithm for high-rate convolutional codes using reciprocal dual convolutional codes is presented. It fulfills all the requirements for iterative (turbo) decoding of parallel concatenated convolutional codes. The computational complexity is low due to the fact that the number of codewords of the low-rate reciprocal dual code is much less than that of the high-rate code. For an efficient implementation forward and backward recursions are introduced.

articleTitle: Two results in text compression algorithms
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We present two results on text compression. One is a general framework incorporating the context sorting algorithm and the LZ77 algorithm. The other is a pre-processor to block sorting which improves its performance when small block sizes are used.

articleTitle: Comparative study of maximum likelihood detection for two multi-rate DS/CDMA systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Multi-rate communication systems are considered for the transmission of direct-sequence code-division multiple-access wireless signals. Performance for jointly optimal detection is studied in the context of multi-code access and variable spreading length access. Prior results for dual-rate systems are extended to multi-rate systems and the effects of correlation between high-rate users in the multi-code scenario are explored. Comparison of the two multirate systems is done via the calculation of asymptotic multi-user performance measures and appropriate bounds.

articleTitle: Some geometric constructions of optimal quaternary codes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: A linear [n,k,d] code over GF(4) is said to be optimal if the minimum distance d is as large as possible for given length n and dimension k. We show that some previously discovered optimal codes have natural geometric constructions. Particular reference is made to optimal [24,5,16] and [46,5,32] codes over GP(4).

articleTitle: A construction of binary BCH convolutional codes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Using BCH block codes and techniques from linear systems theory we present a class of binary convolutional codes with a designed minimum distance.

articleTitle: Reed-Solomon codes meet the error exponent of the asymptotic uniform symmetric channel
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Reed-Solomon codes meet the error exponent of the uniform symmetric channel for all permissible values of the symbol error probability and code rate when the number of channel inputs tends to infinity.

articleTitle: Common randomness and secret key generation with a helper
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Ahlswede-Csiszar (1993) and Csiszar (see Problemy Peredacii Informatsii, 1996) have addressed problems of determining the common randomness (CR) capacity and the secret key (SK) capacity for a variety of models as they arise in information theory and cryptography. We study problems of common randomness and secret key generation by a pair of terminals called the "users" with help from a third terminal, called the "helper". Noiseless one-way communication from the helper to the users as also from one user to the other, subject to rate constraints, is permitted over public channels. A situation involving a wiretapper is also considered.

articleTitle: MAP tailbiting decoders
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: The output of a MAP decoder is the probability of various data symbols and encoder states, rather than the symbol or state itself. The input is the channel observations and the a priori data distribution. For trellis decoding and Markov data, the MAP decoder becomes the BCJR algorithm. The algorithm as given by Bahl et al. (1974) requires that the starting and ending states of the trellis be known, or at least assigned a priori probabilities. With a tailbiting encoder, these quantities cannot be known. The tailbiting technique, in which the starting state of the encoder is set equal to its eventual ending state, improves the decoder error probability when the code word length is short, without the rate reduction that occurs with encoder termination bits. Until now, the BCJR algorithm and tailbiting have not been compatible techniques. This has meant that methods such as turbo decoding and Hagenauer's (see IEEE Trans. Communications, vol.COM-43, p.2449-57, 1995) source-controlled decoding could not be combined with tailbiting encoders.

articleTitle: Computationally efficient turbo decoding with the bi-directional Viterbi algorithm (BIVA)
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: An algorithm for decoding parallel concatenated codes (turbo codes) that replaces the BCJR algorithm with a new Viterbi type algorithm is presented. Replacement of the BCJR algorithm with the new algorithm results in a gain in computational efficiency with only a slight loss in BER performance.

articleTitle: Nonparametric decentralized sequential detection
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We consider a decentralized sequential detection problem with a set of sensors and a fusion center. Each sensor receives information from inputs and possibly other sensors at discrete times and transmits summary information to a fusion center which processes the summary information by performing a sequential test to make a decision on one of two hypotheses. The work discussed differs from previous work by Veervalli, Basar and Poor (1993) in that the conditional densities given each hypothesis are unknown. Information about making good decisions is learned from observing real data and employing reinforcement learning procedures.

articleTitle: Forward error correction with reduction of peak to average power ratio of QPSK multicarrier signals
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Based on complementary sequences, a block coding scheme which reduce the peak to average power ratio (PAPR) of multicarrier signals is considered, and evaluated over a nonlinear channel. Computer simulation results show that with the proposed scheme, considerable improvement can be achieved.

articleTitle: Universal codes and unimodular lattices
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Bonnecaze, Calderbank and Sole (see IEEE Trans. Inform. Theory, vol.41, p.366-77, 1995) introduced for primes p/spl equiv//spl plusmn/(mod8), codes /spl Qscr/ and /spl Nscr/, the universal extended quadratic residue codes, of length p+1 over the 2-adic integers Z/sub 2/spl infin//. For positive integers s they consider their reductions /spl Qscr//sub 2s/ and /spl Nscr//sub 2s/ modulo 2s; /spl Qscr//sub 2/ and /spl Nscr//sub 2/ are just the standard binary extended quadratic residue codes, while /spl Qscr//sub 4/ and /spl Nscr//sub 4/ are the quaternary quadratic residue codes. Given a code C of length n over Z/sub 4/ define /spl Lambda/(C) as the set of vectors in Z/sup n/ which reduce modulo 4 to elements of C. We show, by means of an explicit isomorphism, that if p/spl equiv/-1(mod 8) and p/spl les/31 then 1/2 /spl Lambda/(/spl Qscr//sub 4/) is isometric to lattice L(/spl Qscr//sub 2/) constructed from the binary quadratic residue code in a manner (construction B plus density doubling) generalizing the original construction of the Leech lattice.

articleTitle: Convolutional codes for partial response channels
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: In this paper, convolutional codes for PR channels constructed as superimposed codes based on punctured convolutional codes are studied. The construction has the property of variable rate coding and unequal error protection.

articleTitle: A class of frequency hop codes with nearly ideal characteristics for multiple-target recognition
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: The problem of construction of a code sequence with good auto- and cross-correlation properties for multiple access communications has received a lot of attention. M-sequences and sequences derived from them solve the problem in the one dimensional space. However, the problem of sequence construction becomes much more complicated when extended to two dimensions as is the case in (1) multiuser radar and sonar systems, and (2) FH-CDMA mobile radio. We introduce new families of FH codes whose construction is not limited to GF(p) but remains valid for GF(p/sup n/). The codes are in fact a cross between the so called Lempel-Golomb (1984) constructions for Costas arrays and various families of n-th order congruence codes. We also describe their 2-D auto- and cross-correlation properties. Our construction produces families of FH codes that falls in what are called extended sonar and Costas sequence.

articleTitle: Exact error probability for convolutional codes with soft decision Viterbi decoding
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: The Viterbi decoding algorithm was proposed as a scheme of decoding convolutional codes, and realizes maximum likelihood decoding. Although a large number of studies have been made on its applications, little is known about its exact error performance. Actually, most of results of error performance studies are based on a bound of error performance or by computer simulation. Only few studies have so far been made for exact analyses, but these results were discussed for hard decisions. In general, it is difficult to exactly analyze the error performance of convolutional codes for soft decisions. The error performance for a high signal-to-noise power ratio (SNR) can be obtained by the error bound, however, little attention has been devoted to the exact error performance for low SNR. In this paper, we propose a new technique for the exact analysis of state probability of convolutional codes with Viterbi decoding. This technique employs an iterative calculation of the probability density function (pdf). The proposed technique gives the exact state probability for low SNR. It can be applied for soft decisions.

articleTitle: Comparison of several receiver structures for trellis-coded GMSK signals: analytical and simulation results
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: The performance of some coherent receivers for trellis-coded GMSK signals is examined. It is shown that for the optimal Viterbi receiver in an AWGN channel the tightness of the analytical bounds on the bit-error probability obtained from an N-state error state diagram depends on the degree of non-uniformity of the scheme. The results of the computer simulations of a M-algorithm receiver and a two-stage receiver with separated demodulation and decoding are also given. It is demonstrated that using the M-algorithm the receiver complexity can be substantially reduced with only negligible performance degradation. It is also shown that the M-algorithm can successfully work in receivers for systems with interleaving/deinterleaving circuits.

articleTitle: A trellis coded modulation scheme with a convolutional processor
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We propose a new trellis coded modulation (TCM) scheme. The proposed TCM is encoded by employing the encoder of a convolutional code C, which is followed by a convolutional processor and a signal mapper. Large free distances can be easily achieved for the proposed TCM. The decoding can be implemented by using the trellis for the convolutional code C with some feedback information.

articleTitle: Soft handoff technique for mobile multi-carrier CDMA systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: A multi-carrier (MC) modulation technique has been incorporated into CDMA systems for reason of high data rate transmission, bandwidth efficiency, frequency diversity, interference reduction and so on. We propose a new signal combining scheme for soft handoff in mobile MC-CDMA systems considering the characteristics of MC-signal in a frequency selective fading channel.

articleTitle: Array codes with progressive redundancy
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: It is observed that although the conventional product code scheme offers very good error protection, it contains excessive redundancy, due to the fact that the "inner" code provides the "outer" code with information on many error patterns that exceed the correction capability of the outer code. A coding scheme is presented where this excess redundancy is eliminated. The savings amount in some cases to a reduction of almost 50% in the number of redundant symbols.

articleTitle: Performance of high diversity multidimensional constellations
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We evaluate analytically the performance of component-interleaved multidimensional constellations over the Rayleigh fading channel. The concept of modulation diversity was introduced by Boutros and Viterbo (see IEEE Information Theory Workshop, Haifa, Israel, 1996) as a way to enhance the error performance of communication systems over the Rayleigh fading channel. Several multidimensional signal sets with high diversity order have been proposed to obtain substantial gains over conventional modulation schemes in a fading environment. Modulation diversity can also be viewed as a special form of signal space coding producing highly efficient (in terms of bandwidth and power) schemes over the fading channel.

articleTitle: On independent set of Lee distance Gray codes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: In a Gray code C, the set of k/sup n/ vectors over Z/sub k//sup n/ is arranged in a sequence such that two adjacent vectors are at a Lee distance one. It is assumed that the first and the last vectors in this sequence are also at a distance 1. Two Gray codes, C/sub 1/ and C/sub 2/, over Z/sub k//sup n/ are said to be independent if two words, a and b, are adjacent in C/sub 1/ (or C/sub 2/), then they are not adjacent in C/sub 2/ (or C/sub 1/). If k/spl ges/3, we can have at most n sets of independent Gray codes; for k=2, this number is [n/2].

articleTitle: Lattice constellations matched to GF(p)
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Signal sets matched to the additive group of GF(p) under the Mannheim distance are constructed. Such constellations are obtained via the ring of algebraic integers of an extension K=Q(/spl radic/d) of Q, Where d=-1 or d=-3. The associated lattice constellations are suitable for Rayleigh fading channels because of their high spectral efficiency.

articleTitle: New results on the expected number of maxima in the normal process envelope
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: A new formula for the expected number of maxima in the normal process envelope is presented. In contrast to the complicated Rice's (1954) formula, our simple formula holds for an arbitrary power spectrum. The key idea is the application of characteristic functions, instead of probability density functions, for computing the expected number of level crossings of a process.

articleTitle: Soft-input soft-output building blocks to construct and iteratively decode code networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Soft-input soft-output building blocks (modules) are presented to construct and iteratively decode in a distributed fashion encoder networks, a new concept that includes, and generalizes, various forms of concatenated coding schemes.

articleTitle: Not all nearest neighbors are equal in bounded distance decoding
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Bounded distance soft decoders guarantee correct decoding at least up to half the minimum Euclidean distance of a code, 1/2 d/sub 0/. Under practical working conditions, performance degradation as compared to optimal decoding-is dominated by the behavior of the decoder outside the (bounded distance) hyper-spheres whose centers are the codewords. We carefully investigate this issue and reveal an interesting phenomenon: there are three different types of nearest neighbors classified according to their affect on the decision region. Simulation results are presented to demonstrate this phenomena.

articleTitle: Minimal trellis diagrams of lattices
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Unlike block codes, the number of distinct paths on the trellis diagrams of lattices (N) depends highly on the selected (trellis) coordinate system. Focusing on N as the measure of complexity, it is shown that the problem of finding a proper trellis of a lattice can be reduced to the problem of finding a proper basis for the lattice. For a lattice /spl Lambda/ with coding gain /spl gamma/ and dimension n, a lower bound of the form [/spl gamma//sup n/2/] on N is derived. A trellis of /spl Lambda/ is called minimal if it achieves the lower bound (or more generally, if it minimizes N). For many important lattices like Barnes-Wall lattices BW/sub n/, n=2/sup m/, the Leech lattice /spl Lambda//sub 24/, D/sub n/, D/sub n//sup /spl perp//, E/sub n/, E/sub n//sup /spl perp//, and A/sub n/, n/spl les/9, we obtain the basis matrices which result in minimal trellis diagrams. For some other lattices like the Coxeter-Todd lattice K/sub 12/, and A/sub n/, A/sub n//sup /spl perp//, n>9, trellises with small values of N (probably not minimal) are obtained. The constructed trellises, which are novel in many cases, can be employed to efficiently decode the lattices via the Viterbi algorithm.

articleTitle: Bandwidth-efficient trellis-coded modulation schemes with prescribed decoding delay
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: A class of trellis-coded modulation schemes whose Viterbi decoder optimally decodes observing a prescribed number of intervals is introduced. For a fixed decoding delay, it is shown that the minimum Euclidean distance of the resulting schemes is upper bounded by that of MSK. Signals that achieve this upper bound and maximize the power within a given bandwidth are found.

articleTitle: Linear programming bounds for codes in infinite projective spaces
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We develop a technique for improving the universal linear programming bounds (ULPB) on the cardinality and the minimum distance of codes in infinite projective spaces FPn/sup -1/ (F=R,C,H). We introduce test functions P/sub j/(FP/sup n-1/,/spl rho/) having the property that P/sub j/(FP/sup n-1/,/spl rho/)<0 for some j if and only if the corresponding ULPB can be further improved by linear programming.

articleTitle: Experimental study of ants numerical aptitude based on the ideas of the information theory
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: In order to obtain food ants had to transmit each other the information about a number of one of 30 branches containing a trough with sugared water. However, the food used to appear at the two definite branches much more frequently than at the rest. It turned out that ants, firstly, are able to change their communicative system in order to co-ordinate the time duration of their communications with the frequency of their occurrence and, secondly, they may add and subtract small numbers when transmitting messages about the number of the branch containing the food.

articleTitle: Generalized minimum-distance decoding in Euclidean-space: performance analysis
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Detailed geometric analysis of decoding regions for GMD decoding is presented. We show that GMD decoding regions are non-convex in essentially all cases of interest. We also prove that these regions are always bounded by hyperplane segments. For d-erasure GMD decoding, we establish the presence of a large number of bounding hyperplanes at distance /spl les/d+1. These results invalidate the estimates of performance derived from the union bound in the case of (multistage) GMD decoding. Alternative probabilistic estimates of, and upper bounds upon, the performance of GMD decoding are developed. Simulation results, for both low-dimensional and high-dimensional sphere packings, are in remarkably close agreement with our probabilistic approximations.

articleTitle: Generalized Lee weights for codes over Z/sub 4/
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: In this paper we propose a definition of what we call the generalized Lee weights of codes over Z/sub 4/ which gives the generalized Hamming weights defined by Bassalygo (1995) for the corresponding binary codes.

articleTitle: Remarks on the MacWilliams identities for higher weights
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We present new forms and a new proof of the MacWilliams identities for higher weights. The proof establishes a link between the support weight distributions and matroid invariants.

articleTitle: Mutual information in the continuous time Gaussian channel
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We derive a general formula for the mutual information in the continuous time Gaussian channel with feedback. Our model of the Gaussian channel is most general among those studied previously.

articleTitle: Algebraic-geometric approach in determining the covering radius of long non-binary BCH codes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We give a short survey about geometric methods in determining the covering radius of long non-binary BCH codes. Three classes of BCH codes are considered depending on the alphabet F/sub q/ (q=p/sup r/, p is a prime): q=3; q is large; and q is small.

articleTitle: Coded partial response CPFSK with ring convolutional codes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: In this paper a combination of the convolutional encoder over ring and the modulator for a partial response continuous phase frequency shift keying (PR-CPFSK) signal is described. The examples of the convolutional encoders over ring connected with modulator for the partial response 8-ary CPFSK signal with modulation index h=1/8 that have interesting properties are presented.

articleTitle: Nonexistence results for spherical 3-designs of small cardinalities
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: A spherical /spl tau/-design on S/sup n-1/ is a finite set such that, for all polynomials f of degree at most /spl tau/, the average of f over the set is equal to the average of f over the sphere S/sup n-1/ (Delsarte et al., 1977). We obtain some restrictions on the structure of spherical /spl tau/-designs with the smallest possible cardinalities in terms of the strength /spl tau/ and the dimension n. In fact, we investigate the distributions of the inner products for such designs. Applications for /spl tau/=3 are shown.

articleTitle: Data compression using deterministic experts
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: As an example of a problem in which data can be described by using experts we consider the storage and transmission of chess master games. The transmission of one move in a given situation may be done by coding this move itself or transmitting the number of the expert who proposes this move. We present a stochastic model for "data compression using deterministic experts" and prove some entropy-related upper and lower bounds.

articleTitle: An outer bound for E-capacity region of broadcast channel giving a new outer bound for capacity region
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: The discrete memoryless broadcast channel without a common message is considered. The outer bound of the E-capacity region in the case of average error probability is constructed. When E/spl rarr/0 we obtain an outer bound for the capacity region. For the deterministic channels this bound coincides with the capacity region found independently by Pinsker (1978) and Marton (1979).

articleTitle: An independent window-access scheme for an input-buffered fast packet switching fabric
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: An independent window-access (IWA) scheme is proposed, and several properties of an an input-buffered fast packet switching fabric with the IWA scheme are given and its performance is analyzed. The results obtained show that the IWA scheme has better performance than the traditional window-access scheme. The computer simulation results are seen to be in good agreement with the analytical results.

articleTitle: Information aging
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We introduce the concept of information aging, and we propose a consistent definition of aging which reduces to the classic results for certain aging functions and whose limiting behavior are consistent. In the classic definition introduced by Shannon, the entropy of a random variable (RV) is an eternal quantity solely dependent on the probability mass function (PMF) of the RV itself. The basic premise of this paper is that the time elapsed between the moment of birth of a random event and the point in time when the event is observed is also of significance in so far as the information content of the event is concerned. In particular, we assume that the observation delay diminishes the information content of an event as measured by its eternal value given by the classic definition of entropy. Obviously, certain events are indeed of eternal value, while certain other events increase their information content with the passage of time. We consider the former type, although we provide definitions whereby the aging function is quite arbitrary and can accommodate all the cases noted.

articleTitle: Finite-memory hypothesis testing with semi-bounded likelihood ratio
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We consider hypothesis testing with a finite memory when the likelihood ratio is semi-bounded. It is shown that a 2-state memory can achieve correct convergence with probability one under one hypothesis but only in probability under the other hypothesis.

articleTitle: A new algorithm for finding minimum-weight words in a linear code: application to McEliece's cryptosystem and to BCH codes of length 511
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: An algorithm for finding minimum-weight words in large linear codes is developed. It is pointed out that the original McEliece (1978) cryptosystem is not secure. We also determine the minimum distance of some BCH codes of length 511.

articleTitle: Analysis of power density spectra for coded modulation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: The power density spectra of various digital transmission schemes are derived analytically, using the theory of Markov chains, and discussed.

articleTitle: The optimal linear worst-case information rate
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We present a new approach to upper bound the worst-case information rate for linear secret sharing schemes. It is easier to apply than existing methods and in all examples considered so far it never leads to worse upper bounds.

articleTitle: Belief propagation in loopy Bayesian networks: experimental results
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We investigate the hypothesis that belief propagation "converges with high probability to the correct decision" on a broad class of loopy belief networks. Experimental results of belief propagation on bipartite graphs, which are the belief networks for turbo codes, are presented.

articleTitle: Analysis of frequency-hopped spread-spectrum multiple-access with M-ary FSK over a Rayleigh fading channel
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Frequency-hopped spread-spectrum multiple-access with M-ary FSK over a Rayleigh fading channel is considered. An explicit expression for the symbol error probability as a function of M, the number of users, the number of sub-bands and the SNR is derived. This is used to compare the performance of different block codes, i.e., binary BCH codes, non-binary BCH codes and RS codes. In particular, the codeword error probability as a function of the spectral efficiency is presented for codes of different rates and with different modulation formats.

articleTitle: Multilevel coding of multiple FFSK
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: In this paper, we propose multilevel coded multiple fast frequency shift keying (FFSK) systems which have asymptotic coding gain (ACG) and decoding complexity advantages with respect to their counterparts given in the literature.

articleTitle: Sensitivity of the rate-distortion function of stationary continuous-time Gaussian processes to non-Gaussian contamination
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Let S(N,Z) be the sensitivity of the rate-distortion function (relative to the mean-square-error criterion) of a continuous-time stationary Gaussian process N=N(t) to non-Gaussian contamination Z=Z(t). We prove that for any entropy-regular process Z the equality S(N,Z)=S(N,Z*) holds, where Z*=Z*(t) is a stationary Gaussian process with the same autocorrelation function as Z. An explicit expression for S(N,Z) in the terms of the spectral densities of N and Z is also derived. We also prove that S(N,Z)=0 for any entropy-singular process Z.

articleTitle: Nonlinear ECG filtering by group normalized wavelet packets
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: The group normalized wavelet packet transform is presented to extract ECG components from the additive noise on time-frequency tilings together with the time-frequency masking technique. FIR filters with linear phase is the natural requirement for anti-aliasing. However, linear phase compactly supported real wavelet packets are non-orthogonal so that coefficients at different scale have correlated redundancy and destroy the energy conservation. We design group-normalization to make our entropy definition follow a comparable standard.

articleTitle: Decoding real DFT codes: activity detection, Wiener estimation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Real number cyclic codewords corrupted by possibly a few large excursions and low levels of roundoff noise in all positions are decoded. The correction algorithm uses a Wiener minimum mean-squared error estimator coupled with an activity detector which only indicates a few positions with large error components. One form of this activity selector employs a modified Berlekamp-Massey algorithm.

articleTitle: The way to the proof of Fermat's theorem
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: In the mid-17th Century Pierre de Fermat stated on the margin of a copy of Diophantine's work the conjecture: there are no natural numbers n/spl ges/3,x,y,z such that x/sup n/+y/sup n/=z/sup n/ (Fermat's last theorem, FLT). In 1993 Andrew Wiles announced the theorem: semi-stable elliptic curves over Q are modular. The present paper explains the meaning of Wiles' theorem, his strategy to prove it, and why it settles Fermat's conjecture. We begin by sketching the history of the attempts to prove FLT which reflect its fascination as a challenge for testing the power of the mathematics available.

articleTitle: The depth distribution-a new characterization for linear codes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We apply the well known operator of sequences, the derivative D, on codewords of linear codes. The depth of a codeword c is the smallest integer i such that D/sup i/c (the derivative applied i consecutive times) is zero. We show that the depth distribution of the nonzero codewords of an [n,k] linear code consists of exactly k nonzero values, and its generator matrix can be constructed from any k nonzero codewords with distinct depths. Interesting properties of some linear codes, and a way to partition equivalent codes into new equivalence classes are also discussed.

articleTitle: Source coding in multimedia
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: A key area of multimedia systems is source coding. We review the state of the art in source coding of speech, audio, image, and video signals, including discussions of both standards-based and nonstandard approaches to coding. We demonstrate, via example, the current compression and coding capabilities of a wide range of algorithms, at various bit rates; for source coding of each of these signals. We also review the unique and challenging issues that face source coding on both wireless and data networks, and discuss the solutions that are currently being investigated.

articleTitle: Mismatched frequency hopping sequences for radars and sonars
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: The authors consider the possibility of sidelobe suppression, i.e. self-clutter suppression in modern radar and sonar systems with intrapulse multilevel mismatched frequency hopping. We achieved interesting results.

articleTitle: Type II codes over Z/sub 4/
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: The conditions satisfied by the weight enumerator of self-dual codes, defined over the ring of integers module four, have been studied by Klemm (1989), then by Conway and Sloane (1993). The MacWilliams (1977) transform determines a group of substitutions, each of which fixes the weight enumerator of a self-dual code. This weight enumerator belongs to the ring of polynomials fixed by the group of substitutions, called the ring R of invariants. Among all of the quaternary self-dual codes, some have the property that all euclidean weights are multiples of 8. These codes are called type II codes by analogy with the binary case. An upper bound on their minimum euclidean weight is given, thereby leading to a natural notion of extremality akin to similar concepts for type II binary codes and type II lattices. The most interesting examples of type II codes are perhaps the extended quaternary quadratic residue codes. This class of codes includes the octacode [8, 4, 6] and the lifted Golay [24, 12, 12]. Other classes of interest comprise a multilevel construction from binary Reed-Muller and lifted double circulant codes.

articleTitle: Large linear complexity sequences over Z/sub 8/
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Construction of binary sequences derived from Z/sub 8/-sequences, under the most significant bit map. These binary sequences are shown to have large linear complexity.

articleTitle: Information reconstruction using minimum number of erroneous patterns and optimization problems of multiple transmission
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: The problem of effectively reconstructing an unknown object using its patterns distorted by errors of given type and multiplicity is considered. The efficiency of recognition is understood in the sense of minimizing the number N of erroneous patterns that are sufficient for reconstructing an unknown object exactly or with given accuracy and/or with given error probability. This problem essentially differs from the traditional problems of storing and transmitting encoded messages, because we consider reconstruction of an arbitrary object from a given set. In this paper the problem is formulated in terms of metric spaces, and it is solved for metric spaces that are most interesting for the theory of information transmission. For these metric spaces, the minimum numbers of erroneous patterns are obtained, and simple algorithms for reconstructing objects using these minimum numbers of patterns are presented.

articleTitle: Improved error probability bounds for a block-coded signal with a bounded decision region in the presence of AWGN
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Bounding techniques for the error probability in detecting a transmitted signal in the presence of AWGN are considered. The error probability, P/sub e/(i), is the conditional probability that the received signal is incorrectly detected assuming that the ith signal was transmitted. Tight upper and lower bounds on P/sub e/(i) in the low SNR region are useful for the performance analysis of some concatenated multilevel block coded modulation schemes which can achieve a high coding gain. We propose a new lower bound which is always tighter than the bounds of Shannon (1949) and Swaszek (see IEEE Trans. Inform. Theory, vol.41, p.837-41, 1995) so that the bound is tight at both high and low SNRs. This so-called improved cone lower bound was derived by combining the bounding techniques of Shannon and Swaszek.

articleTitle: New authenticated key distribution scheme and secure broadcast scheme
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We make use of [2nl+1,nl+1] systematic MDS code over GF(2/sup m/), m being a positive integer no less than 64, to construct a new authenticated key distribution scheme with the ability to correct t errors, which may distribute simultaneously a session key k among n users. To protect the integrity of message, a message authentication check symbol is also introduced into the new scheme.

articleTitle: New sufficient conditions for decoding optimality and regions containing the optimal codeword
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Consider a binary linear block code that is used for error control over an AWGN channel using BPSK transmission. This paper presents three sufficient conditions that either assert the optimality of a suboptimally decoded codeword or define a small region which contains the optimal (or most likely) codeword. A new minimum-weight-trellis search based iterative decoding procedure using these sufficient conditions for optimality is proposed. Simulation results for well known codes of lengths up to 64 show that the new sufficient conditions for optimality are very effective for finding the optimal codeword. The new iterative decoding procedure results in low computational and implementation complexity.

articleTitle: Practical implementations of cryptography
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Dicusses public key systems including their general nature, their problems and the model within which these systems can be realized. The application to electronic commerce, home banking and the Internet are discussed.

articleTitle: Quasi-cyclic array codes are equivalent to shortened Gilbert codes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Zhang and Wolf (1988) determine the burst correction capability of a n/sub 1//spl times/n/sub 2/ quasi-cyclic array code with parameter s. It is shown that this code can be obtained from a n/sub 3//spl times/n/sub 2/ Gilbert code for some n3>n/sub 1/, by shortening. This construction leads to simple expressions for the burst correction capability and allows burst correction by error trapping.

articleTitle: A concatenated random error and burst erasure decoding scheme for random noise and burst fading or interference channels
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: A concatenated random error correction and burst erasure recovering code scheme is proposed. This will significantly improve the performance of communication systems in some applications. This proposal is based on an efficient erasure decoding algorithm for binary block codes and an efficient application in the presence of fading or interference.

articleTitle: Source coding theorem for an extended Slepian-Wolf system with two interactive decoders
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: The author considers an extended Slepian-Wolf system which has two decoders although the original Slepian-Wolf System has only one decoder. It is assumed that source outputs are i.i.d. but they are mutually correlated and the decoders communicate with each other via rate-restricted noiseless channels. Using the coding theorem derived the transmission rates of the decoders are examined.

articleTitle: All Z/sub 4/ codes of Type II and length 16 are known
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Using a new computer algorithm that determines the automorphism group of a Z/sub 4/ code, and efficient ways to find generator matrices of Type II codes, we show that there are 133 inequivalent Type II Z/sub 4/ codes of length 16.

articleTitle: On generalized Hamming weights for Preparata codes over Z/sub 4/
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We determine the rth generalized Hamming weight d/sub r/(m) of the Preparata code of length 2/sup m/ over Z/sub 4/ for r=0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3.0 and any m/spl ges/3. For m=3, 4, 5, 6, and m=7, the weight hierarchy is completely determined except for d/sub 4/(7).

articleTitle: On the classification of binary sequences of period 2/sup n/-1 with ideal autocorrelation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Several new miscellaneous sequences with ideal autocorrelation are found in a closed-form expression using the trace function up to a period 2/sup 23/-1. The number of inequivalent binary sequences in each category is listed, including newly found miscellaneous sequences.

articleTitle: Carrier suppressed RAKE receiver operation for CDMA cellular communications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: The paper presents a way to operate the RAKE receiver in a CDMA cellular communication system without the aid of the unmodulated cell unique PN, i.e., the pilot for the purpose of increasing the capacity with less transmission power. The receiver operation with suppressed carrier was accomplished simply through first despreading one known Walsh code, then wiping out the user's data either by noncoherent energy measurement in timing tracking or by taking ratio of I and Q channel estimation in coherent demodulation.

articleTitle: A low complexity soft-output decoder for a broad class of trellis coded modulation schemes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: This work introduces a general concept to extend the principles of soft output Viterbi decoding to M-ary transmission. The proposed algorithm matches ideally the family of punctured pragmatic TCM (P/sup 2/-TCM) schemes. Due to the puncturing technique employed, such a decoder can be realized by a basically traditional SOVA with a slightly modified metric and time-variant labeling, operating at a multiple clock speed.

articleTitle: On the information-theoretic capacity of discrete-time queues
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We analyze the information-theoretic capacity of two models of discrete-time queues, one involving single arrivals and single service in a slot, and the other involving batch arrivals and batch service. We explicitly specify the capacity-minimizing service distributions for both models, and obtain the resulting timing capacities.

articleTitle: On the minimum distance of certain cyclic codes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We characterize several classes of cyclic codes of length 2/sup m/-1 which have minimum distance three. We are mainly interested in codes with generator m/sub i/(x)m/sub j/(x), but we also treat the cases when the generator polynomial is a product of several polynomials m/sub i/(x).

publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory

articleTitle: Author index
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: The author index contains an entry for each author and coauthor included in the proceedings record.

articleTitle: Minimum energy in information transmission
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: It is shown that the minimum energy required to transmit a natural unit of information (nat) over a noisy channel is kT, where T is the effective noise temperature which depends on the interaction between the information career and the environment. The result follows from the entropy defect principle and general laws of quantum dynamics without any specific assumptions.

articleTitle: A study on difference of codelengths between MDL codes and Bayes codes on case different priors are assumed
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We analyze quantitatively the the difference of codelengths between both codes for the hierarchical (nested) model class.

articleTitle: Information-theoretic bounds on trellis complexity of nonlinear codes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Information-theoretic measures are used to derive both upper and lower bounds on the state complexity and on the branch complexity of nonlinear block codes To the best of our knowledge, the proposed upper bounds are the only upper bounds that address nonlinear codes. The improvement of the novel lower bounds is twofold: these bounds are tighter than the existing bounds and they also bound the trellis complexity of improper and unobservable trellis diagrams, unlike the existing bounds.

articleTitle: Reliability and throughput analysis of ARQ schemes in burst error channels
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Block codes are often used in combination with a retransmission strategy to establish an automatic repeat request (ARQ) scheme. The fundamental schemes are stop-and-wait (SW), go-back-N (GBN), and selective repeat (SR) ARQ. Clearly, a performance analysis of an ARQ scheme has to include a suitable channel model. We present an analytical method for evaluating the reliability and throughput of ARQ schemes in burst error channels. An algebraically decoded linear block code is utilized for error detection. The proposed approach leads to closed formulae for reliability and throughput.

articleTitle: Pseudoredundant measurements in nonlinear mappings
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We show, that additional measurements, created by some mathematical formulas, do provide additional information about state space variables, when the mapping from the state space into the observation space is nonlinear.

articleTitle: Multi-track codes for magnetic recording systems with servo positioning errors
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We consider designing multi-track codes to combat inter-track interference and servo positioning errors. We show that coding gains between 3 dB to 4.8 dB are attainable without compromising from the high rates desired in various applications.

articleTitle: Probability density function of the line-of-sight angle error
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: The closed form probability density function (PDF) of the angle between the input and output of the time discrete AWGN channel is derived. Two N-dimensional Cartesian systems are considered. The PDF can be used for calculation of the corresponding cumulative distribution function (CDF) which determines the best known general lower and upper bounds on the decoding error probability of optimal block codes on the AWGN channel. For odd values of N/spl ges/3 this reduces to a closed form too.

articleTitle: Evaluation of TCM transfer functions for recursive Ungerboeck codes using QAM modulation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Transfer function expressions for recursive Ungerboeck TCM codes using QAM modulation over AWGN channels are derived under the condition of uniformity: computer results are given for 4-state and 16-state encoders.

articleTitle: Whitening sequences in DS spread spectrum communication
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: This paper is devoted to the investigation of a spectrum dependence on pseudo noise (PN) sequences and their cross-correlations in direct sequence spread spectrum (DS/SS) communication systems.

articleTitle: Codes combining error detection and authentication
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We introduce codes that combine error detection and authentication, and show that such combining codes are superior to codes providing error detection and authentication independently.

articleTitle: The capacity of orthogonal and bi-orthogonal codes on the Gaussian channel
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: This paper analyzes the performance of concatenated coding systems operating on the additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channel by examining the loss of capacity resulting from each of the processing steps. The described techniques allow the separate evaluation of codes and decoders and thus the identification of where loss of capacity occurs. Knowledge of this capacity loss is useful in the overall design of a communications system, e.g., for evaluating the benefits of inner decoders that produce information beyond the maximum likelihood (ML) estimate. The development of this paper is restricted to orthogonal and bi-orthogonal codes operating on the AWGN channel; however, the methods have wide application and can be used to assess arbitrary codes on other channels.

articleTitle: New ternary nonlinear codes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We present two ternary nonlinear codes showing that A/sub 3/(12,7)/spl ges/45 and A/sub 3/(13,7)/spl ges/87. Codes with such parameters were not known until now.

articleTitle: Large s-box design using a converging method
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: IA new technique is presented for the construction of substitution boxes (s-boxes). This has been developed in response to the need for a fast algorithm for obtaining large s-boxes with good properties. Because of the speed of the algorithm, many good s-boxes can be constructed quickly, with the best of these chosen for use based on a test of their cryptographic properties.

articleTitle: A low-complexity and high-performance concatenated coding scheme for high-speed satellite communications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: This paper presents several concatenated coding scheme for high-speed satellite communications. The NASA Standard (255, 223) Reed-Solomon (RS) code over GF(2/sup 8/) is used as the outer code and a Reed-Muller (RM) code is used as the inner code. A simple trellis diagram with parallel structure for the RM code is devised. This concatenated scheme achieves high-performance with high decoding speed and low complexity.

articleTitle: A vector quantizer for additive white and colored Gaussian noise channels
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Most of the work on joint source-channel coding deal with discrete channel models. We investigate the design of joint source-channel coding scheme for continuous-amplitude channels. More specifically, we propose a channel-optimized vector quantizer (COVQ) for additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) and additive colored Gaussian noise (ACGN) channels with soft-decision binary phase-shift keying (BPSK) modulation.

articleTitle: A necessary and sufficient condition for partition testing to be better than random testing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: A necessary and sufficient condition is given for partition testing to be better than random testing. A simple strategy is given to maximize the probability of success of partition testing.

articleTitle: Modularity properties of graph entropy
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Graph entropy is an information theoretic functional on a graph and a probability distribution on its vertex set. It is sub-additive with respect to graph union but not submodular in general. Here we give necessary and sufficient conditions on graphs for sub- and also for supermodularity of graph entropy with respect to every probability distribution.

articleTitle: On pattern frequency occurrences in a Markovian sequence
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Consider a given pattern and a random text generated by a Markovian source of any order. We study the frequency of pattern occurrences in a random text when overlapping copies of the pattern are counted separately. More precisely: we consider two strings, a given pattern string H=h/sub 1/h/sub 2/....h/sub m/ and a random text string T=t/sub 1/t/sub 2/...t/sub n/ of respective lengths equal to m and n over an alphabet S of size V. The results for the Markovian model are summarized in two theorems.

articleTitle: Reed-Solomon error control coding in multichannel FSK coherent lightwave systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: (n,k) Reed-Solomon codes can effectively reduce the impact of laser phase noise and relax the required optimum IF expansion bandwidth in a dual-filter FSK optical communication system. The coding gain increases as the channel separation is reduced, and the error probability floor can be eliminated. The required IF expansion bandwidth and sensitivity can be reduced substantially as the coding gain predominates.

articleTitle: Convex duality and the value of side information
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Let X be a random variable with distribution P on a measurable space /spl chi/. A function q*(x) is log-optimum in a convex family /spl Qscr/ of nonnegative measurable functions on /spl chi/ if it attains the maximum growth exponent W/sub /spl Qscr//(X)=sup/sub q(xin/spl Qscr/)/E{log/sub q/(x)}. The analysis of random variable with joint distributions generalizes to the setting of stationary processes and log-optimum selections in multiplicative sequences of convex families.

articleTitle: Non-linear codes for joint source- and channel-coding
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: A new tight lower bound on the word error rate for the coded transmission of redundant data over discrete memoryless channels is derived and compared with other known bounds. Furthermore, we deduce from this new bound that the optimal error correcting code is in general non-linear and give its distance profile.

articleTitle: Zero-error capacity for models with memory and the enlightened dictator channel
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Summary form only given. We present a general class of "combinatorial" 0-error capacity problems with the "memory" covering known and many new cases. This class can be incorporated into a model of channels with memory. W analyse a seemingly basic channel in this class, which we call the "dictator channel". Clearly, a dictator always follows his own opinion. However, we speak of an enlightened dictator, if he responds to the unanimous vote of the people against his opinion to the degree, in this case he reaches a decision by coin tossing.

articleTitle: On associative nets
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We consider the Boolean model of associative memory using neural nets. The previous results from the superimposed code theory are applied to obtain exchange relations between the model parameters and the size of stored information.

articleTitle: An algebraic geometric single key cryptosystem using stream ciphers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: A new single key cryptosystem is proposed based on binary algebraic geometric (AG) Goppa codes and secure stream ciphers. The system provides both security and the capability of correcting channel errors. The keystream generator is selected to provide a high level of security. The error control code provides channel error correction as well as an extra level of security by including the actual code selected as part of the key. This is distinct from previous schemes using error control codes where errors are added before transmission. We describe two models for our cryptosystem.

articleTitle: Active distances and cascaded convolutional codes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: A family of active distances for convolutional codes is introduced. Lower bounds are derived for the ensemble of periodically time-varying convolutional codes.

articleTitle: Enumeration of rare events, pyramid and ball cubic lattices
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We give each binary word of length n with p ones, p/n/spl rarr/0, a code whose length asymptotically by 1.56 bits per one exceeds the minimum. The encoding and decoding speed counted in operations over bits is maximal to within a constant factor. So, we trade length for speed. We present similar algorithms enumerating the pyramid and ball cubic lattices.

articleTitle: A CELP-based speech-model process controlled by trained Markov chains
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: A novel speech-model process (SMP), which is based on a modified CELP-structure, is proposed as a test signal for speech processing applications. The applied CELP-structure and the generation procedure for this SMP are presented. The controlling part of this SMP involves several kinds of Markov chains to adapt the time-varying properties of the process to those of natural speech. The measurement results have shown that the characteristics of "Markov-CELP"-SMP agree well with those of natural speech. This concept renders it possible to produce a test signal with characteristics of several languages and/or to generate a test signal which includes required special features if needed, like male/female-type speech or weak/strong variation of pitch frequency.

articleTitle: The initial efficiency of investment for the general market
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We investigate how one invests in the stock market X when there is a rate constraint on the side information V. The doubling function /spl Delta/(R) is the maximum increase in the doubling rate when V is described to the investor at rate R. The initial efficiency /spl Delta/'(0) is the largest possible increase in the doubling function per bit of description. We introduce the linearized maximal correlation and use it to provide a lower bound for the initial efficiency. We also show that the initial efficiency is bounded above by the square of the Hirschfeld-Gebelein-Renyi maximal correlation between the side information V and the market X. We can use these bounds to find the initial efficiency for V=X and for the horse race market.

articleTitle: Cyclic subcodes of generalized Reed-Muller codes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We define homogeneous generalised Reed-Muller codes (HRM codes). These are subcodes of the generalized Reed-Muller (GRM) codes. We show, that while they have less information symbols, there is a significant increase in the minimum distance. HRM codes are also naturally related to projective Reed-Muller codes (PRM codes). In particular, we can deduce their parameters from the PRM codes. We show, that punctured HRM codes are cyclic, while PRM codes in general are not. Hence, HRM codes compare favorably to both GRM codes and PRM codes. We show that binary trace codes of q-ary HRM codes are well-defined and give their parameters. The trace codes include codes that have the same length and minimum distance as some classical RM codes, but with a significant increase in the dimension.

articleTitle: Fibre products of superelliptic curves and codes therefrom
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We construct new families of smooth projective curves over a finite field F/sub q/ with a lot of F/sub q/-rational points. The genus in every such family is considerably less than the number of rational points, so the corresponding geometric Goppa codes have rather good parameters. Let X be a smooth projective curve of genus g=g(X) defined over a finite field F/sub q/. The Goppa construction of linear [n,k,d]/sub q/-codes associated to the curve X is described.

articleTitle: Data-punctuated token trees
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Summary form only given. In the problem we consider, one party (the "receiver") seeks to obtain a copy of a large file or unstructured database from another party (the "source") over a communication link which is slow or expensive relative to the computing power available at each end. The communication link is bi-directional, and error-free in both directions, although it may have delay. The receiver has an outdated version of the source file. Although there may have been many changes between these two large files, they are still substantially the same, in the sense that many large portions of the file were unaffected by the changes. For ease of exposition, we treat the file as a single long sequence of n symbols. The goal is an algorithm which ends when the receiver has constructed an identical copy of the source file, and which reaches this state after transmitting an amount of data proportional only to the sum of the sizes of the changes, and some terms proportional to log n. In other words, when n is very large, the amount of data communicated should be negligible compared to n, assuming reasonably large agreement between the two versions of the file. We achieve this goal. Cyclic redundancy checks (CRCs) play an important role in this algorithm. The least significant byte of each CRC is called a token. The novel notion in this paper is a very simple new data structure, which we call a data-punctuated token tree. For each of the two files, this tree is constructed independently, starting from the leaves and ending with the root. When completed, each node in this tree contains a token on an appropriate subsequence of the data and a punctuation bit. The punctuation bits, which are derived from the data, define the structure of the tree.

articleTitle: An adaptive projection receiver for asynchronous coded CDMA
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: An adaptive realization of a reduced-complexity multiuser detector for asynchronous CDMA signals is presented. This detector, termed the projection receiver, is a near-far resistant statistical interference canceller which combines error control decoding with multiuser interference resolution. Theoretical performance bounds, simulation results, and adaptive implementation algorithms are presented.

articleTitle: D/sup 2/-ary signaling for incoherent all-optical CDMA systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: A new method for two-dimensional multi-ary signaling in optical networks is presented, which combines two signaling schemes, D-ary PPM and D-ary FSK. Jointly with code-division multiple-access (CDMA), higher data rates than in conventional CDMA systems and larger network sizes can be achieved. Also fewer frequencies than in wavelength division multiplexing (WDM) are required.

articleTitle: A class of low-complexity line codes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: A unified family of novel and existing single added bit line codes is presented. These can offer reasonably good line coding characteristics with a minimum increase in complexity.

articleTitle: Good universal codes can be obtained by concatenated codes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: This paper investigates the error correcting capabilities of concatenated codes with time-varying randomly selected constant composition inner codes. It is proved that such code can achieve Gallager's (1968) random coding error exponent for all rates, while both encoding and decoding of the codes do not depend on the channel.

articleTitle: A study of performance and decoding complexity in lattice codes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: The decoding complexities and coding gains at finite error rates of a number of Barnes-Wall lattices and their sub-lattices have been estimated, and the performance/complexity trade-off compared with that of the Leech lattice.

articleTitle: Error correction for semiconductor memories
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We discuss an error correction method that is applicable to semiconductor memories for which the majority of errors is already present immediately after writing. Decoding can be performed much more easily than with an equally powerful conventional error correcting code.

articleTitle: Linear codes and the two-way chain condition
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: A necessary and sufficient condition for a q-ary code to satisfy the two-way chain condition (TCC) is found. A known construction is shown to lead to codes which satisfy the TCC. Some q-ary codes of dimension k/spl les/6 meeting the Griesmer bound are proved to satisfy the TCC.

articleTitle: A new class of codes for byte organized systems from algebraic curves
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: A new class of linear codes over GF(q) for byte organized systems from algebraic curves is proposed. Here, an element in GF(q) is called a symbol and "byte" denotes a q-ary sequence of length b/spl ges/2. A codeword in the code is composed of n bytes of byte-length b, thus, the code-length is nb, where N:=nb. These codes have the capability of correcting any error that corrupts both t/sub 1/ bytes and t/sub 2/ symbols within another byte where t/sub 2/<b. We call such a code a t/sub 1/ byte and t/sub 2/ symbol error correcting code, or a (t/sub 1/Bt/sub 2/S)EC code. Moreover, we refer to an error that corrupts both t/sub 1/ bytes and t/sub 2/ symbols within another byte as a t/sub 1/ byte and t/sub 2/ symbol error.

articleTitle: PPM multibits/sequence-period optical orthogonal CDMA systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: This paper proposes M-ary PPM-OCDMA combined with an F-ary multibits/sequence-period optical orthogonal CDMA system (F is the sequence period). We derive the performance of the proposed system. It is shown that the proposed system achieves log/sub 2/FM/log/sub 2/M times higher throughput, keeping the advantages of power efficiency and low bit error rate.

articleTitle: Structured spherical codes for Gaussian quantization
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We construct a vector quantizer for the Gaussian source which outperforms known existing quantizers for rates above 2 bits per sample, and of equivalent computational complexity. In particular it outperforms "trellis-based scalar-vector quantization" and "trellis coded quantization". The quantizer is a gain-shape quantizer, whose shape codebook consists of a "wrapped spherical code" in 25 dimensions, constructed from the Leech lattice in 24 dimensions.

articleTitle: A Nordstrom-Robinson based concatenated block coding scheme for the (1-D) partial-response channel
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: This paper examines the performance of the nonlinear Nordstrom-Robinson (NR) code on a dicode partial-response channel. A concatenated coding scheme consisting of a NR code and the biphase code without precoder gives a significant improvement of the free squared Euclidean distance, d/sub free//sup 2/, as compared to the Hamming distance-driven lower bound for the precoded (1-D) channel.

articleTitle: Rotationally invariant, geometrically uniform trellis codes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Given a group trellis and a partitioned signal set, we show how to find all geometrically uniform mappings from the trellis branches to the partition cells. The result is a procedure for constructing geometrically uniform trellis codes and a simple test for rotational invariance.

articleTitle: Trellis-canonical generator matrices for convolutional codes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
